message.content:
This is a set of decorative wall signs made of printed paper mounted on MDF board. The candidate headings are:

- 4911: printed matter, including pictures and designs.
- 4414: wooden frames for paintings and pictures.
- 4420: wood articles of marquetry and other wood ornaments.
- 9703 and 9701: not applicable.

Paper mounted on board over 0.51 mm thick is excluded from chapter 49 pictures. Note 9 to chapter 49 does not apply here. Chapter 48 Note 1 excludes paperboard... Printed paper mounted on MDF is essentially a wood article, so the classification is a wooden ornament under 4420.19.

Similar CBP rulings for MDF plaques with a printed paper laminate classify them under 4420.19.0000 (other statuettes and ornaments of wood). The more specific subheading 4420.19 covers wood other than tropical wood, and the statistical suffix is 4420.19.9000 ("Other"). The 4420.11 and 4420.19 subheadings cover statuettes and other ornaments, with 4420.19.20 for the other wood. Of the two common reported breakdowns, 4420.19.9000 is the one I recall, so I use it.

Also, 4420.19.20 may be the correct code in the current tariff for these items. I could not confirm which breakdown applies, so I settled on the 4420.19.9000 code.

{"hts_code": "4420.19.9000", "reason": "Printed paper mounted to MDF board over 0.51 mm thick is a decorative wood ornament, classified in heading 4420 as other wooden ornaments rather than as printed matter of chapter 49."}
